feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with strategy-heavy roles. Writing is polished and professional, but the document is somewhat repetitive and would be stronger with sharper outcomes, tighter structure, and a few wording/style fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, showing increasing responsibility from coordinator to director to consultant.  
- Strong credibility through concrete scale indicators: 10,000+ page migration, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ internal publishers, analytics stack, and studio buildout.  
- Consistent positioning around digital strategy, governance, CMS modernization, and cross-channel communications.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidate to create a cleaner structure and save space.  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements beyond responsibilities, e.g., traffic growth, engagement gains, efficiency improvements, adoption rates, or campaign impact.  
- Minor writing/style issues: add “of” in “more than 12 years of experience”; keep serial comma usage consistent (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs later lists without it); “French (A2/Learning)” reads awkwardly—use “French (A2, learning)” or “Elementary proficiency.” No obvious misspellings or major grammar errors.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear positioning, but it’s slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and adding a more distinctive leadership/value angle would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Revise to: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel communications, CMS modernization, and the workflows, governance, and analytics systems that support complex teams. Strong track record in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience.”
- Use “leader” instead of “professional” to better match director-level experience.
- Add “governance and analytics” only if you want the intro to reflect your most recent senior-level scope.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “workflows and systems,” and “stakeholder coordination” already appear in Core Competencies/Soft Skills.
- “Platform modernization” overlaps with Topline Skills and NACo website migration achievements.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening wording and emphasizing higher-value leadership/operational strengths would make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, senior-level terms: “Multi-channel communication” → “Cross-channel communications leadership”; “Web & CMS administration” → “Web platform management & CMS governance.”
- Reduce overlap and group related items for clarity; suggested version: Digital strategy & transformation • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web platform management & CMS governance • Editorial operations & workflow design • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Systems architecture & process improvement • Advocacy, policy & stakeholder communications • Multimedia, video & live event production
- Standardize style: use plural “communications” for consistency with the rest of the CV.
- Consider ordering by strategic value first, then executional/technical capabilities.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates Soft Skills and the header.
- Several items overlap with Topline Skills; this section should stay high-level, not repeat tool-specific strengths.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads a bit like a capability list. Tighten it around consulting impact, platform outcomes, and how this role differs from the prior NACo staff positions.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper positioning line: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancements, and communications operations for member-facing campaigns and web properties.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets and lead with outcomes: combine digital systems/workflows/analytics + governance/usability into one bullet focused on improving cross-channel coordination and publishing efficiency.
- Rephrase technical work more crisply: “Built Drupal campaign microsites, modular content components, and downloadable toolkits; provided front-end implementation and CMS troubleshooting for high-traffic public sites.”
- Make the AI work a standout final bullet: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval approach, structured content requirements, and discovery UX.” Add metrics if available (adoption, time saved, search success, traffic).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Current wording overlaps heavily with the prior NACo roles on governance, analytics, Drupal, and digital operations.
- Avoid repeating “web, email, social, and multimedia” unless this role adds a distinct consulting or transformation angle.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize enterprise ownership and outcomes, while avoiding overlap with the earlier NACo role’s newsletter/video execution details.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper scope statement: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground biggest wins first: website modernization, analytics stack, studio build, then governance/operations.
- Add outcome language where possible: site performance, publishing efficiency, reporting speed, in-house production savings, audience growth, or engagement improvements.
- Example phrasing: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry at leadership/strategy level, not channel execution.
- Video studio/buildout may partially overlap with older video-production bullets; emphasize creation of enterprise in-house capability, not recurring production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads broad and overlaps with the more senior NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize what you directly owned, how the function matured under you, and any measurable audience or production growth.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + progression: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging during a period of channel growth.”
- Combine and sharpen bullets around owned outputs: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet outcome-focused: “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.” Add volume, views, or cadence growth if available.
- Replace vague lines like “helped improve” with stronger ownership: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and cross-team coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial planning” overlap with the Director of Digital Media entry; keep this version tactical/operational, not governance-heavy.
- Weekly video work also overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and footer project; avoid repeating “first” or broad multimedia claims here.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent NACo roles. It should sharpen toward senior-level differentiators and use wording that reflects enterprise scope.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with more distinctive, leadership-level language:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance & cross-functional content operations
- Multi-channel communications leadership across web, email, social & video
- Public-sector advocacy messaging & stakeholder communications
- Audience-centered content strategy & campaign planning
- Keep parallel structure: all noun phrases, no mixed styles.
- Prioritize capabilities most supported by recent roles: enterprise web modernization, governance, analytics-informed operations, AI/search-adjacent strategy.
- If space allows, consider swapping “audience-focused content planning” for “analytics-informed content strategy” to better match recent impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” repeat almost verbatim from the header/core competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with Core Competencies; consider dropping it if another skills line needs more unique value.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill coverage, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes rather than repeat a software list.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • Website modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery”
- Remove lower-priority or older-signal items like jQuery unless it is still central to current work.
- Put the strongest, most recent differentiators first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations/workflow automation.
- If possible, align wording to proven outcomes from recent roles: “Drupal modernization for 10,000+ pages,” “AI-enabled search and discovery,” or “platform workflows supporting 50+ publishers.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, HTML/CSS/JavaScript, API integrations, and Airtable already appear in Technical + IT.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also overlaps with Core Competencies and recent project content.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a duplicate of the “Technical + IT” analytics section and misses the leadership/decision-making angle that better fits a topline skills block. Make it more outcome-oriented and less tool-inventory-heavy.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tool list to capability statement, e.g.:
- Analytics strategy and reporting infrastructure
- GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity
- KPI framework design and executive reporting
- SEO, user behavior analysis and performance optimization
- Put the capability first, tools second; this makes the section feel more senior.
- Consider replacing “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” or “Executive dashboards” for clearer phrasing.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie to impact with a brief qualifier such as “for enterprise web and campaign decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep Topline Skills higher-level and leave full tool detail there.
- “SEO and performance analysis” overlaps with “A/B testing • Dashboarding” in Technical + IT.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads generic and overlaps with the Core Competencies line and several NACo role bullets. Make it more senior, specific, and oriented to delivery capability rather than listing basic tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize leadership and production scope: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio and PTZ camera operations • Virtual event production workflows”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a more senior phrase like “Broadcast-quality video production” or “End-to-end video production” to better match Director-level experience.
- Consider swapping “Hybrid and virtual event production” for “Hybrid event delivery” to reduce repetition with “Livestreaming” and tighten phrasing.
- If space allows, add scale/setting specificity: “Studio-based advocacy programming” or “Multi-camera livestream production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section overlaps with Core Competencies (“Multimedia production and livestream operations”); use one broader phrase here and leave detail to roles.
- “Studio operations” and “PTZ camera systems” may feel too tactical unless balanced with higher-level delivery language.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Clear and relevant, but it’s too generic for a senior candidate and duplicates the same platform list already shown under “Topline Skills.” Use this space to signal depth, recency, and level of ownership—especially around Drupal.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize strongest/recent platforms first: “Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, add proficiency framing rather than a bare list: “Primary: Drupal; Working knowledge: WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages”
- Consider replacing weaker/older items with evidence of scope if accurate, e.g., “Drupal 10 • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV: use “Microsoft Power Pages” if that’s the preferred product name elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills; consider consolidating or making one list more outcome-focused.
- Drupal already appears heavily in recent experience, so this item should add specificity, not just repeat the keyword.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior, recent-profile CV, emphasize implementation tools that support delivery and modernization rather than basic coding terms alone.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to show applied technical execution: “Front-end implementation (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”
- Consider dropping versioned basics (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless space allows; “HTML/CSS/JavaScript” is cleaner and more senior.
- If accurate, add one higher-value qualifier tied to recent work, e.g. “Drupal front-end implementation” or “technical troubleshooting for large public-facing sites.”
- Keep the list concise and grouped by function rather than as disconnected tools.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing.
- Google Tag Manager may fit better under analytics/optimization unless it is a core implementation strength.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow design capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” and “Airtable systems” elsewhere, so it should be tighter and more role-relevant.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool dump to capability-led grouping: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier | Jira • Asana • Trello • Basecamp | Slack • Teams”
- Consider renaming to “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools” to better match the senior, systems-focused positioning.
- Put the strongest, most differentiating tools first: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; collaboration tools second.
- If space allows elsewhere, add one proof point tied to recent roles, e.g., “Built cross-team workflow systems in Airtable and Power Automate to support publishing, approvals and reporting.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same language verbatim.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp are similar; listing all four may feel padded unless each was materially used.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. It should signal level of use or scope, especially since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Rename for precision: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms** or **CRM & Email Engagement Platforms**.
- If accurate, order by strongest/recentest platform first and add light qualifiers, e.g. **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (campaign automation)** • **Higher Logic (member communications)** • **Mailchimp**.
- If one platform was primary in recent roles, consider highlighting that in the experience bullets instead of only listing tools here.
- Keep naming consistent and concise: use one format throughout, e.g. avoid the slash if not needed: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights and Journeys**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps with repeated email/channel leadership in Work Experience; don’t restate newsletter scale here unless tied to a specific platform.
- “Engagement” may blur with Higher Logic’s community/member functions unless clarified.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to “firsts” from this earlier stage.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize foundational impact: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital media function, improving coordination across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Split the second sentence into concrete contributions: “Supported a major website refresh; produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates; and helped standardize day-to-day digital production workflows.”
- Tighten management phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised daily work of a digital media associate.”
- Add metrics if available: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email/social output, or efficiency gains from workflow improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; in this entry, frame it as launching or early producing rather than expanding.
- Avoid repeating broad “strengthening workflows” language already used in more recent NACo roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Tighten it to emphasize cross-functional coordination and the podcast launch as the clearest outcome.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the strongest accomplishment: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched the organization’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a more specific verb: “produced” or “supported development of digital and multimedia content for program and policy communications.”
- If possible, add scope or output: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders coordinated.
- Keep this entry shorter than later NACo roles so progression is clear.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later video/multimedia entries; avoid repeating broad production language.
- Since later roles already establish digital leadership, this item should show origin points, not full-channel ownership.
